name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.06
notes: The watch: ESP32-S3R8 (8 MB octal PSRAM) in a wrist form factor with a 410x502 CO5300 AMOLED on QSPI, FT3168 capacitive touch, QMI8658C 6-axis IMU, PCF85063ATL RTC and an AXP2101 PMIC, all sharing one I2C bus on SDA=15/SCL=14. Audio is the same ES8311-out/ES7210-in pair as the AUDIO-Board, so codec_init.cpp already knows the chip — but the pins differ and the NS4150B amp enable is a direct GPIO (46) here rather than living behind an I/O expander, which makes the speaker one pin away instead of an I2C transaction. Two things this board has that no earlier profile did: a screen, and a power management chip. The AXP2101 gates rails, so a build that assumes peripherals are powered at boot may find the codec silent for reasons that are not the codec's; bring the PMIC up before blaming the audio path. The display is here now that a firmware layer exists to consume it: the panel is driven as an SH8601 over quad SPI — the wiki calls the controller CO5300, but Waveshare's own BSP drives it with the SH8601 driver and a panel-specific init sequence, and the panel is the thing that has to agree. Its column address starts at 22, hence x_offset; the panel is mounted a half turn from its natural orientation, hence rotation 180, found by eye on the bench rather than from a drawing; the FT3168 touch controller shares the I2C bus with everything else.

audio_in.notes: Dual digital microphone array sharing the ES8311's MCLK/BCLK/LRCK. Not yet driven by the firmware, though the pins are all it needs: the AUDIO-Board drives the same ES7210 as of 2026-08-26, so building for this board should mostly be a matter of trying it.
